cells.tense: You are in it right now, and your hands are steady.
cells.verb: letting the finished thing be finished, and trusting what comes after it
cells.place: the doorway you've already stepped through, standing in the open air on the other side
cells.ask: offer one ending that feels complete an easy, unhurried goodbye — and let what comes back be the fairness of the exchange, given and received without tallying.
cells.core:
You're clearing what's finished, and you're not arguing with it. The ending came because something in you knew it was time, not because you forced it — and the release is clean because you let it be clean. What you're making room for, you haven't met yet, and you're at peace with that.

The clearing has a fairness to it that you didn't have to construct. You gave what was yours to give and you let go of the rest, and the balance holds on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting what's finished be finished, and trusting what comes after.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for the next ending before this one has landed.
cells.verb: burning down what's still standing instead of letting it end on its own time
cells.place: ahead of yourself, at a door that hasn't closed yet, ready to force it
cells.ask: let one thing stay with you a day longer than the fear wants — and let what comes back be the recognition that holding on and letting go are both yours to choose, without needing to fuse with anyone to prove it.
cells.core:
You're clearing things before they've had their life. The upheaval feels like liberation — each ending feels like the one that will finally free you — but you're ending on fear's schedule, not on the thing's own. The next ending won't settle what this one was for.

What you're actually moving away from can't be outrun by moving faster. Some of what you're ending still has something to give you.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending things before they've had a chance to live.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already closed behind you.
cells.verb: holding what's already gone, calling it loyalty
cells.place: the old room, the one whose light you keep on for no one
cells.ask: let one thing move — not the big thing, just one — and what comes back will be direction from what you actually feel, not from what you think you owe.
cells.core:
Something in your life is already over and you're keeping it upright. The holding feels like faithfulness, like you're being the kind of person who doesn't abandon, but the loyalty is pointed at something that isn't there anymore. The room is dark. You're the only one still in it.

The energy it takes to keep the dead thing standing is the same energy that would carry you into whatever's next.
cells.sheetLine: Something's already over and you're keeping it upright.

cells.tense: Something in you is ending right now, and you're still writing it into the column of things that are steady.
cells.verb: being cleared from below, without knowing it
cells.place: in the middle of a release you haven't named, in a body that already knows
cells.ask: say 'this is ending' about one thing you've been counting on — and let what comes back be the quiet structure underneath, the thing that holds when the ground shifts.
cells.core:
You're describing your life as stable, but something in it has already begun to let go. The ending is happening — in how your body moves, in what you reach for and don't, in the small relief you feel when you're not doing the thing. You haven't said it yet, so it doesn't have a shape.

The release is already running. It just doesn't have your name on it yet.
cells.sheetLine: Something's ending in you, and you're still calling it steady.
